translations.text: Again, an account of the passing of Saint John the Apostle and Evangelist.
Now Saint John was with the blessed brothers, rejoicing and delighting in the Lord.
On the following day, which was Sunday, when the brothers were gathered together, he began to speak:
“My brothers and companions, heirs and partners in the kingdom of Christ, you know how much God has given you through my hands:
how many signs, how many wonders, how many gifts, comforts, ministries, teachings, acts of guidance, favors, and honors.
How many things you see before your eyes being given to you, which cannot be seen by these eyes or heard by these ears!
Therefore stand firm in him, remembering him in every work of theirs and understanding the mystery of the saving plan that took place among human beings,
and why it took place. The Lord asks this of you. Indeed, through my hands the Lord asks and urges you, my brothers, wishing us to remain without giving offense,
without deceit, without filth. For he knows the insult that comes from you; he knows contempt. For he knows the insult that comes from you; he knows contempt.
He knows humility. He knows how to punish when you do not obey his holy commandments. Do not,
therefore, let your good God be grieved: he who is gracious, merciful, holy, and undefiled;
he who alone is, who is unchanging, true, without deceit, and not prone to anger;
he who is exalted above every name that you can utter or conceive—Jesus, who is God.
Let him therefore rejoice as you conduct yourselves well and live purely. Let him be glorified as you conduct yourselves innocently.
Let him not [?] when you join together. Let him be glorified in your chastity. Let him rejoice as you love him. I say these things to you, my brothers,
as I hasten toward this appointed task, which is already being fulfilled in the Lord. For what is there to say to you? You have the dwelling of God.
You have the pledge of his grace. You have his coming, from which there is no excusing yourselves.
If, then, you no longer sin, those things that without knowledge—then you no longer sin:
those things you did without knowledge he forgives you. But if, even while you know him and have received mercy from him,
you conduct yourselves in similar ways, those former things too are counted against you, and you have no share in him, O friends.”
After saying these things to them, he prayed as follows: “Jesus, you who wove this wreath with your own weaving,
you who joined these many flowers to your own flower that never falls, you who sowed these words of yours,
you alone are compassionate toward your servants, a physician who heals freely; you alone serve without arrogance; Jesus, you alone are gracious and merciful.
In your grace, shelter all who hope in you, you who know the schemes and plundering of the adversary.”
Then, having asked for bread, he prayed as follows: “What praise, or what offering,”
Or what thanksgiving shall we offer you as we break bread? Rather, to you alone, Jesus Christ, we give thanks—to the name of the Father that has been spoken.
We praise your entrance through the door. We praise the resurrection that was proclaimed to us through you. We praise your word, your glory,
your indescribable pearl, your treasury, your net, your greatness, the one who for our sake was called the Son of Man, the truth, knowledge, rest,
power, the commandment, boldness, and the freedom that is in you. For truly you are the Lord who was called the root of immortality
and the spring of incorruptibility and the foundation of the worlds. Therefore we acknowledge your greatness, which is now invisible.
After he had broken the bread and stretched out his hand to them, and had prayed over everyone that they might be worthy of the grace that is in the Lord, and also of the holy Eucharist,
he too tasted it and said, “I too likewise have a share with you, and peace and love.”
Then he said to Byrrhus, “Take with you two brothers who have baskets and spades, and come after me.”
Byrrhus, without delay, carried out what John, the servant of God, had commanded him.
Then the blessed John went out of the house and walked in front of the gate. He told the many people to move away from him.
When he came to the tomb of one of our brothers, he said to the young men, “Dig, my children.” And they began digging.
He stood over them insistently and said, “Let the pit be deep.” And while they were digging,
he spoke the word with them and encouraged them with him, along with those who had come out of the house,
while [?] and speaking to them about the greatness of Christ, and praying over each one of them.
When those young men had finished the pit as he wanted, while we knew nothing, he took off the clothes he was wearing
and laid them like bedding down in the depth of the pit. Standing in only his cloak, he raised his hands and prayed as follows:
“God, who chose us to be apostles to the nations, you who sent us into the world, you who revealed yourself through your apostles,
you who never ceased [?] from the people's deceptions, but always saved those who were able,
you who made yourself known through all nature, and proclaimed yourself even among the animals, you who made the desolate soul that had become savage peaceful
and restful, you who gave yourself to it when it thirsted for your word, you who quickly appeared to it when it was dead,
you who alone appeared to it when it was drowning in sin, you who immediately revealed yourself to it when it was overcome by Satan,
you who did not allow it to live according to the flesh, you who showed it its enemy, you who created pure joy,
God, Jesus, Father of those above heaven, Lord of the heavenly beings, God of the heavenly beings, and law of those in the ether,
the course of those in the air, guardian of those on earth, the fear of earthly beings, and the peace of those who are his: receive the soul of your John,
so that [?] he may be found worthy before you, Jesus, you who have also kept me pure for yourself until this hour, untouched by union with a woman.”
You who appeared to me in my youth [?], when I wanted to take a wife, and said to me, “I need you, John.”
You who sought me for [?] bodily procreation, when three times, in my disobedience, I wanted to undertake it.
You who said to me on the sea, “I need you, John. Otherwise,
I would have allowed you to take a wife, to mourn and weep.” You who in the third year opened the eyes of my mind,
and granted me my physical eyes. You who made it difficult for me to look at a woman and gaze at her. You who rescued me from the illusion of this age, and for that which bears fruit continually
kept me. You who rescued me from the madness of fleshly impurity. You who separated me from bitter death and established me in dependence on you.
You who rebuked the hidden disease of the [?] and put an end to its harsh activity. You who constrained and drove beyond the boundary the one who was stirring up turmoil within me.
You who kept my love for you unstained. You who granted that my journey toward you should be without stumbling.
You who inscribed in me pure knowledge of you. You who give each worker a fitting reward.
You who put it into my soul to possess nothing but purity. For what can I now find that is better than you, Lord?
I have fulfilled the great stewardship entrusted to me. Make me worthy of your rest, granting me perfection in you.
You who are salvation beyond description and expression. As I journey toward you, let the fire retreat. Let darkness be overcome. Let the pit lose its strength.
Let the furnace be stunned. Let Gehenna be quenched. Let angels accompany me. Let demons be afraid. Let the rulers [?]. Let the powers of darkness fall.
Let the places on the right stand, but let those on the left not stand. Let the devil be silenced. Let Satan be mocked. Let his toil be undone.
Let his glory be disgraced. Let his anger be brought to nothing. Let his children be struck down. Let his whole root be torn out. But make my path toward you free from dishonor and
plunder, and let me receive what you promised to those who lived purely and loved you alone.
He turned toward the east and offered praise, standing wholly in the light, and said, “Be with me, Jesus Christ our Lord.”
Then he went down into the pit where he had laid his clothes. After saying to us, “Peace and well-being to you, my brothers,” he joyfully gave up his spirit. May his prayer be with us. Yes.
The account concerning John the Evangelist is finished. May his prayer be with us. Amen.
